applied.summary: Added missing possessive: 'a brass instrument's valves make' (grammar). FK 7.2.
Added missing possessive: 'a brass instrument's valves make' (grammar). FK 4.9.
Changed 'across the courses' to 'across the strings'; web-verified the standard prima balalaika has three single strings (E4-E4-A4), not doubled courses.
Removed redundant 'quickly back and forth ... and rattles' wording; tightened to 'brushes the strings in rapid up-and-down strokes, producing a continuous, tremolo-like brrr'.
Removed 'Course (paired strings)' (balalaika uses single strings, not courses); list now 5 items, within 3-6 spec.
Aligned romanization in definition ('zou shou yin') to the term header ('zou yin'); 'zou yin' (走音) is an attested variant for the sliding/stopped tones. Term field left unchanged.
Replaced tension-implying rubber-band analogy with a length-based trombone-slide analogy so the image reflects a positional slide, not a bend. FK 6.3.

Changed 'octave and twelfth' to 'twelfth (xylophone) or double octave (marimba and vibraphone)'; web-verified (euphonics.org / Fletcher & Rossing) that bars are tuned to 3:1 or 4:1, never a 2:1 octave.
Disambiguated the noise-source list: 'mechanical hum, bearing rattle, or brush-and-commutator buzz' (serial comma + hyphen) so the three sources are distinct.
Split the garbled run-on 'sounded by striking the block over its slit and rounder and softer...' into two clean sentences (raised by two experts).

Corrected which reed sounds: overblow (exhale) sounds the draw reed with the blow reed choked; overdraw (inhale) sounds the blow reed with the draw reed choked. Web-verified (Wikipedia 'Overblowing'; opening/closing-reed mechanism).
Replaced redundant 3rd item (duplicated item 1) with a distinct, verified voicing mistake about over-strong chiff giving a hard, exaggerated attack (Britannica 'nicking'; CB Fisk).
Added sibling entries 'Organ wind noise' and 'Pipe hiss' for navigation; swapped out 'Reed noise' and 'Attack transient' to keep the list at 6 (3-6 spec).
Fixed garbled modifiers 'the freely, uncontrolled vibrating reed' to 'the freely vibrating, uncontrolled reed'.

declined.reason: Declined. 'Head-locked' is a recognized immersive-audio term a student would encounter, and the proposed gloss ('a source fixed to the screen/front that does not move even when the head turns') is ambiguous: 'does not move even when the head turns' reads naturally as world-locked, the OPPOSITE of head-locked (which stays fixed relative to the head). It also risks contradicting the entry's own definition of listener-relative. I could not confirm a precise, differentiating gloss to the required authoritative-source standard (only blogs/forums available), so adding it would risk introducing a new error, which the rules forbid.
